observations: Photo 0: A black Xbox 360 Slim console with visible 'XBOX 360' logo on top, a matching wireless controller resting on it, and a power brick connected with a lit green LED.
Photo 0 shows wires running behind the console suggesting it's hooked up, but no cables to a TV are clearly traceable.
Photo 1: A TV screen displaying an eFootball 2024 start menu, implying some console is powered and running a game, but the console itself is not visible in this shot.
No close-up of any console label, serial number, or hard drive capacity sticker is provided.
No view of the disc tray, rear ports, or any visible wear/scratches on the shell.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 confirms it is an Xbox 360 Slim by the visible logo, but no photo shows a 250GB label or storage info.

claims.claim: Fully working and in good condition
claims.evidence: Photo 1 shows a game menu on a TV, which could suggest a working unit, but there is no clear link (same frame, cable, or room continuity) proving this console in photo 0 is the one powering that screen.
Photo 0 shows a power brick with a lit LED connected to the console, but nothing confirms it is the original Microsoft unit versus a third-party replacement.

risks.risk: Storage capacity may not actually be 250GB as claimed
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the hard drive or console sticker showing capacity

risks.risk: Console may have disc read errors or not power on fully (common 360 Slim fault)
risks.proof: Video of console booting to dashboard and reading a disc

risks.risk: Power supply may be a non-original replacement, affecting resale/safety value
risks.proof: Photo of power brick showing Microsoft branding and model number

risks.risk: Unseen wear, cracks, or overheating damage (yellowing, dust buildup) on the shell
risks.proof: Multiple angle photos in bright light showing all sides of the console

risks.risk: Controller sync and condition (stick drift, button wear) unconfirmed
risks.proof: Video demonstrating controller function on the console

proof_requests: A video showing the console powering on, reading a game disc, and the controller functioning, filmed continuously in the same room as the TV shown.
A clear photo of the console's underside or hard drive sticker showing the storage capacity.
A photo of the power brick showing brand markings to confirm it is an original Microsoft supply.
Additional photos of the console from multiple angles in good lighting to assess cosmetic condition.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as an Xbox 360 Slim console from the visible branding, but functionality, true storage capacity, and originality of the power supply are all unverified, so it must be priced at worst case pending proof.
